zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qamar
Meccan
﷽
﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾: the exegetes are agreed — and we have narrated it from trustworthy people of knowledge — that the moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abū Isḥāq «[Translator's note: i.e. al-Zajjāj himself.]» said: A group who have strayed from the right course and from what the people of knowledge hold claimed that its interpretation is that the moon will split on the Day of Resurrection. But the matter is clear from the wording and from the consensus of the people of knowledge, because of His saying: ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2] — so how could this be at the Resurrection?
Abū Isḥāq said — and all that is dictated to you on this is what Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq narrated to me — he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Minhāl narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas: «that the people of Mecca asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, so he showed them the moon twice — its splitting», and he used to mention this hadith at this verse: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Qatāda, from Anas, who said: "The moon split into two parts."
Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Ḥirmī ibn ʿUmāra narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪd «[Translator's note: so in the source; possibly a misprint for Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd.]» narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Anas, who said: «"The people of Mecca asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, and the moon split in Mecca twice, and He said: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]"», meaning: passing away. Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr narrated to us, he said: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "The moon split, and I saw the mountain between the two gaps of the moon." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh — concerning His saying ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — he said: "The moon split until I saw the mountain between the two halves of the moon." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: «"The moon split while we were with the Prophet ﷺ at Minā, until one part of it went behind the mountain, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba and Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, and from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from Abū Masʿūd, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Prophet ﷺ into two parts, one part above the mountain and one part below it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Masʿūd «[Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel chains have Musaddad.]» narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿUmar, the like of it. Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ informed us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Abī Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two pieces, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'Bear witness, bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī said — and he narrated it to us another time — from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: «"The moon split into two pieces, so that we saw it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Kathīr narrated to us, from Sulaymān — meaning Ibn Kathīr — from Ḥuṣayn, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two parts, on this mountain and on this mountain, and the people said: 'Muḥammad has bewitched us.' A man said: 'If he has bewitched you, he has not bewitched all the people.'"» And Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Three things that Allah has mentioned in the Qurʾān have already come to pass: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — the moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two pieces, so that the people saw it." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, he said: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās — concerning His saying ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — he said: "It happened before the Hijra: the moon split, so that they saw its two pieces." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr said, from ʿIkrima, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the idolaters said: 'The moon has been bewitched, the moon has been bewitched!' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrima: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the idolaters said: 'The moon has been bewitched, the moon has been bewitched!' So there came down: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿĀrim ibn al-Faḍl and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib «[Translator's note: so in the source; the name ʿIkrima in this chain looks out of place.]», from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who said: "I set out with my father on Friday, and Ḥudhayfa addressed us — and Sulaymān said in his narration: Ḥudhayfa gave the sermon while he was at al-Madāʾin — and he recited ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾, then said: 'Indeed, the Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race.'" Sulaymān said in his narration: "So I said to my father: 'O father, will the horses be set loose tomorrow?!'" And ʿĀrim said in his narration: "So I said to my father: 'Will the people race tomorrow?!' When the following Friday came, he addressed us and recited ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ and said: 'Indeed, the Hour has drawn near, and the moon split in the time of your Prophet ﷺ. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race; the goal is the Fire, and the winner is the one who races to Paradise.'" Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥabīb, who said: "We were at al-Madāʾin and came to the Friday prayer, and Ḥudhayfa addressed us. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'To proceed: Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race; indeed, the goal is the Fire.' When the next Friday came, he addressed us; he praised Allah and extolled Him" — he said — "and said the like of what he had said, and said: 'The winner is the one who races to Paradise.'" Ismāʿīl narrated to us: ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Sulaymān and Qaṭar «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably Fiṭr.]», from Muslim, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "The inescapable punishment (al-lizām) has passed, the great seizure (al-baṭsha) has passed, the smoke (al-dukhān) has passed, and al-Rūm (the Romans) has passed." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Ibn Zayd said: "The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and half of it was seen on Quʿayqiʿān and the other half on Abū Qays «[Translator's note: i.e. Mount Abū Qubays, so written in the source.]»."

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ فانْتَصِرْ﴾: the reading is ﴿أنِّي﴾ with fatḥa on the alif, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar the grammarian read "إنِّي" with kasra on the alif. Sībawayh explained "إنِّي" with kasra, saying: it is on the intention of "saying" (qawl), in the sense of: "So he called upon his Lord and said: 'I am overcome.'" He said: and similar to it is ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أوْلِياءَ ما نَعْبُدُهم إلا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ زُلْفى﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]; the meaning is: "They said: 'We only worship them so that they may bring us near.'" And whoever reads with fatḥa — and that is the proper way — the meaning is: "He called upon his Lord with [the words] that I am overcome."

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying: ﴿فَفَتَحْنا أبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾: the meaning is: "So We answered his supplication and helped him." And He made clear the help with which he was helped, saying: ﴿فَفَتَحْنا أبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾: pouring down violently.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿وَفَجَّرْنا الأرْضَ عُيُونًا﴾: this is the majority reading, ﴿عُيُونًا﴾ with ḍamma; it has also been transmitted as "عِيُونًا", with kasra on the ʿayn, and that is poor in Arabic.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فالتَقى الماءُ عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾: meaning the water of the sky and of the earth. He did not say "fa-ltaqā l-māʾāni" (the two waters met), though had it been so it would have been permissible; but "الماءُ" is a noun that comprises the water of the earth and the water of the sky. The meaning of ﴿عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾ is: which had been decreed in the Preserved Tablet. And it has been said: "قَدْ قُدِرَ" means the amount of the sky's water was like the amount of the earth's water.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَحَمَلْناهُ عَلى ذاتِ ألْواحٍ ودُسُرٍ﴾: the meaning is: "on a ship made of planks". "اَلدُّسُرُ" is the name for the nails and the cords with which the planks are bound. Everything like nailing, or driving one thing into another with force and great compulsion, is "دَسْرٌ"; one says "dasartu l-mismāra, adsuruhu, wa-adsiruhu" (I drove in the nail). "اَلدُّسُرُ": its singular is "دِسارٌ", like "حِمارٌ" and "حُمُرٌ".

zajjaj:14-14.t:
And His saying: ﴿لِمَن كانَ كُفِرَ﴾, that is: We did that as a recompense for Nūḥ and his companions, that is: We saved him and those who believed with him, and drowned those who denied him, as a recompense for what was done to him.
And His saying: ﴿تَجْرِي بِأعْيُنِنا﴾, that is: it sails within Our sight and under Our protection.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْناها آيَةً﴾, that is: We left this deed and the matter of Nūḥ's ship as a sign, that is: a mark from which a lesson may be taken. ﴿فَهَلْ مِن مُدَّكِرٍ﴾: the reading is with the undotted dāl. Its origin is "مُذْتَكِرٌ", with dhāl and tāʾ, but the tāʾ was replaced by dāl — and the dhāl is from the place of articulation of the tāʾ, and is closer to the dāl than to the tāʾ — and then the dhāl was assimilated into the dāl. This is the proper way, I mean the reading with the undotted dāl. Some Arabs said "مُذَّكِرٍ", with the dotted dhāl, assimilating the second into the first; but this is not the proper way — the proper way is assimilating the first into the second.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾, that is: passing away; and it has been said: lasting.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكُلُّ أمْرٍ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾: its interpretation is that the deeds of the people of the Fire become settled for them, and the deeds of the people of Paradise become settled for them.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَهم مِنَ الأنْباءِ ما فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ﴾: meaning of the reports of those who went before them and were destroyed for their denial. ﴿ما فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ﴾, that is: that in which there is a restraint. You say: "nahaytuhu fa-ntahā" (I forbade him and he desisted) and "zajartuhu fa-zdajara" (I rebuked him and he refrained). The origin is "fa-ztajara", with tāʾ, but when the tāʾ comes after a zāy it is replaced by a dāl, as in "مُزْدانٌ", whose origin is "مُزْتانٌ", and likewise "مُزْتَجَرٌ". It was replaced by a dāl only because the tāʾ is a voiceless (mahmūs) letter and the zāy a voiced (majhūr) letter, so in place of the tāʾ there was substituted a voiced letter, namely dāl. This is understood only by one who has mastered the whole of Arabic, and it is at the end of the Book of Sībawayh. What should be said to the learner is: when you form "اِفْتَعَلَ" or "مُفْتَعَلٌ" from a root whose first letter is zāy, change the tāʾ into a dāl, as in "اِزْدَجَرَ" and "مُزْدَجَرٌ".

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حِكْمَةٌ بالِغَةٌ﴾: "حِكْمَةٌ" is nominative as a badal (substitute) for "ما"; the meaning is: "And there has come to them far-reaching wisdom." And if you wish, you may make "حِكْمَةٌ" nominative with "هُوَ" implied; the meaning is: "It is far-reaching wisdom."
And His saying: ﴿فَما تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾: "ما" may be interrogative in form with the meaning of rebuke, so that the meaning is: "So what do the warnings avail?!", and its position would be accusative by "تُغْنِ". And it may be a negation, in the sense of: "So the warnings do not avail."

zajjaj:6-6.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهم يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدّاعِ إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾: the complete pause (waqf al-tamām) is at ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾.
And His saying ﴿إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾: to what they used to deny of the resurrection. "So turn away from them; on the day [such-and-such happens]" as in the verse «[Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]». "يَوْمَ" is accusative by His saying ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الأجْداثِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 7]. As for the omission of the wāw from "يَدْعُ" in the written text, it is because it is dropped in pronunciation owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters, namely the wāw of "يَدْعُو" and the lām of "اَلدّاعِ"; so it was written as it is pronounced. As for "اَلدّاعِ", retaining the yāʾ in it is better, though omitting it is permissible, because the kasra indicates it.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خُشَّعًا أبْصارُهُمْ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "They come out of the graves, their eyes humbled." It has also been read "خاشِعًا أبْصارُهُمْ", and Ibn Masʿūd read "خاشِعَةً أبْصارُهُمْ". With active participles, when they precede a plural, you may use the singular, as in "خاشِعًا أبْصارُهُمْ"; you may use the singular with the feminine, because of the femininity of the group: "خاشِعَةً أبْصارُهُمْ"; and you may use the plural, as in "خُشَّعًا أبْصارُهُمْ". You say: "marartu bi-shubbānin ḥasanin awjuhuhum" (I passed by young men handsome of face), "ḥisānin awjuhuhum" and "ḥasanatin awjuhuhum". The poet said:
؎وَشَبابٍ حَسَنٍ أوْجُهُهم ∗∗∗ مِن إيادِ بْنِ نِزارِ بْنِ مَعَدِ
(And young men handsome of face, of Iyād son of Nizār son of Maʿadd.)

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ إلى الدّاعِ﴾ is also accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "They come out, their eyes humbled, مُهْطِعِينَ." The meaning of ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ is: staring, not lifting their eyes away.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
And His saying: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهم قَوْمُ نُوحٍ﴾, that is: the people of Nūḥ denied Nūḥ before your people, O Muḥammad.
﴿وَقالُوا مَجْنُونٌ وازْدُجِرَ﴾: and they said "He is mad", just as your people said of you, O Muḥammad ﷺ, and upon them all.
"وازْدُجِرَ": he was rebuked with abuse. We have already explained what there is in "مُزْدَجَرٌ" concerning the change of the tāʾ into a dāl; the origin of this is "وازْتُجِرَ".

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنا القُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ﴾: the meaning is "We have made it easy". And it has been said: the books of the followers of other religions — such as the Torah and the Gospel — are recited by their followers only by looking at the text, and they hardly memorise their books from beginning to end as the Qurʾān is memorised.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا﴾: "صَرْصَرًا" means intensely cold.
﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ﴾: meaning "نَحْسٍ" (ill-omened), and "مُسْتَمِرٍّ" means lasting in its ill omen. And it has been said: on a Wednesday at the end of the month that does not come round again.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَنْـزِعُ النّاسَ كَأنَّهم أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾: "كَأنَّهُمْ" here is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "It plucks the people out, resembling uprooted palm trees." Al-munqaʿir is that which is cut off from its roots; the wind would throw them down on their faces.
And His saying: ﴿مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾: "النَّخْلُ" (palm trees) is treated as masculine and feminine; one says "hādhā nakhlun" and "hādhihi nakhlun". So "مُنْقَعِرٌ" follows those who say "hādhā nakhlun"; and for those who say "hādhihi nakhlun", it is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ خاوِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 7].

zajjaj:23-23.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾: "اَلنُّذُرُ" is the plural of "نَذِيرٌ" (warner).

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿فَقالُوا أبَشَرًا مِنّا واحِدًا نَتَّبِعُهُ﴾: "بَشَرًا" is accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb, which the overt one explains; the meaning is: "Shall we follow a human being?!"
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا إذًا لَفي ضَلالٍ وسُعُرٍ﴾: its meaning is: "Then we would indeed be in error and madness." One says "nāqatun masʿūra" (a crazed she-camel) when she has madness. And it may be in the sense of: "If we follow him, we are in error and in torment."

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying: ﴿بَلْ هو كَذّابٌ أشِرٌ﴾: "أشِرٌ" is in the sense of "بَطِرٌ" (insolent, arrogant). One says "ashira, yaʾsharu, asharan, fa-huwa ashirun", like "baṭira, yabṭaru, baṭaran, fa-huwa baṭirun".

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا مُرْسِلُو النّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ﴾: "فِتْنَةً" is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "We are sending the she-camel in order to try them", that is: to test them.

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهم أنَّ الماءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهم كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ﴾, that is: the water is divided between the she-camel and Thamūd: she has a day and they have a day. And this is its meaning: "Every drinking turn is attended: the people attend the drinking one day, and the she-camel attends one day."

zajjaj:29-29.t:
﴿فَنادَوْا صاحِبَهم فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ﴾: he used to be called "Aḥmar Thamūd" (the Red One of Thamūd) and "Uḥaymir Thamūd" (the little Red One of Thamūd). The Arabs err and make him "Aḥmar ʿĀd", and use him as a proverb for ill omen. Zuhayr said, describing a war:
؎فَتُنْتِجْ لَكم غِلْمانَ أشْأمُ كُلُّهم ∗∗∗ كَأحْمَرِ عادٍ ثُمَّ تُرْضِعْ فَتَفْطِمِ
(It will bear for you sons of ill omen, all of them like the Red One of ʿĀd; then it will suckle and wean.)
And the meaning of ﴿فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ﴾ is: he undertook the hamstringing of the she-camel, and he hamstrung her, and so attained what he wanted.

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً فَكانُوا كَهَشِيمِ المُحْتَظِرِ﴾, with kasra on the ẓāʾ; and it is also read "اَلْمُحْتَظَرِ", with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ. "اَلْهَشِيمُ" is leaves that have dried up, broken and crumbled; that is: they became like the dry stubble which the owner of the enclosure (al-ḥaẓīra) gathers, that is: it had reached the utmost dryness, to the point of being gathered to be burned. Whoever reads "اَلْمُحْتَظَرِ" with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ, it is a noun for the enclosure; the meaning is: "like the stubble of the place in which stubble is enclosed". And whoever reads ﴿المُحْتَظِرِ﴾ with kasra on the ẓāʾ, it is a reference to the one who gathers the stubble of firewood in the enclosure, for he is "اَلْمُحْتَظِرُ", because he is the agent.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إلا آلَ لُوطٍ نَجَّيْناهم بِسَحَرٍ﴾: "سَحَرٍ", when it is indefinite, meaning some pre-dawn time or other, is declinable (fully inflected, munṣarif). You say: "ataytu Zaydan saḥaran mina l-asḥār" (I came to Zayd at a pre-dawn time). But if you mean the pre-dawn of your current day, you say: "ataytuhu li-saḥarin yā hādhā" «[Translator's note: so in the source, with nunation; given the point being made, the intended form is presumably diptote, li-saḥara.]» and "ataytuhu saḥara yā hādhā" (I came to him this pre-dawn, you there).

zajjaj:35-35.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿نِعْمَةً مِن عِنْدِنا﴾ is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "We saved them in order to bestow favour upon them." Had it been read "نِعْمَةٌ مِن عِنْدِنا" (nominative), it would be a valid way, and the meaning would be: "That is a favour from Us; Our saving them is a favour from Us." Abū Isḥāq said: But I know of no one who read it so, so do not read it so unless a sound transmission is established. Our teachers among the people of knowledge said: Reading (qirāʾa) is a followed practice (sunna muttabaʿa), and they do not hold that anyone may read according to what is permissible in Arabic if no sound transmission is established.

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ فَطَمَسْنا أعْيُنَهُمْ﴾: the people of Lūṭ tried to seduce Lūṭ away from his guests, who were the angels. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded Jibrīl, and he struck their eyes with his wings with a single stroke, took them away and effaced them, and they remained in the house blind and bewildered.

zajjaj:38-38.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهم بُكْرَةً عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾: "بُكُرَةً" and "غُدْوَةً" (early morning), when they are indefinite, take nunation and are declinable; but when you mean by them the early morning of your current day, you do not make them declinable. So "بُكْرَةً" here is indefinite. Had it been read "بُكُرَةَ عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ" and "نَجَّيْناهم بِسَحَرَ نِعْمَةً مِن عِنْدِنا", both would have been permissible in Arabic, the meaning being "the early morning of their day" and "the pre-dawn of their day". But the indefinite, declinable form is better in this verse, and no transmission has been established that it was on such-and-such a day of such-and-such a month.

zajjaj:43-43.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أكُفّارُكم خَيْرٌ مِن أُولَئِكُمْ﴾, that is: are your disbelievers, O company of Arabs and those to whom the Prophet ﷺ was sent, better than those — that is, the disbelievers whose stories and destruction We have mentioned? ﴿أمْ لَكم بَراءَةٌ في الزُّبُرِ﴾, that is: or has it come to you in the scriptures that you are absolved of what would necessitate your ʿidāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source (عداءكم, "enmity towards you"); possibly a misprint for عذابكم, "your punishment".]»?

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُنْتَصِرٌ﴾: the meaning is: "Rather, do they say: 'We are a united host, victorious', and so presume upon strength and unity against you?!"
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He would destroy them from the very direction from which they reckoned on victory, and said: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, that He would make him prevail over them and make His word the highest, saying: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]; and this defeat was on the day of Badr.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
And His saying: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾: the meaning is "and they will turn their backs (al-adbār, plural)", as He said: ﴿وَإنْ يُقاتِلُوكم يُوَلُّوكُمُ الأدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 111]. Likewise is the meaning in His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في جَنّاتٍ ونَهَرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 54]; the meaning is "in gardens and rivers". The singular noun indicates the plural, and is made to suffice for the plural. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl recited:
؎بِها جِيَفُ الحَسْرى فَأمّا عِظامُها ∗∗∗ فَبِيضٌ وأمّا جِلْدُها فَصَلِيبُ
(In it are the carcasses of exhausted camels: as for their bones, they are white, and as for their skin, it is hard.)
They mean "and as for their skins (julūduhā)". And he recited:
؎فِي حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقَدْ شُجِينا
(In your throat is a bone, and we have choked.)
The meaning is: in your throats are bones. And as he said:
؎كُلُوا في بَعْضِ بَطْنِكم تَعِفُّوا ∗∗∗ فَإنَّ زَمانَكم زَمَنٌ خَمِيصٌ
(Eat with part of your belly and stay restrained, for your time is a time of hunger.)
The meaning is: "Eat with part of your bellies."

zajjaj:46-46.t: Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهم والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾, that is: the killing and captivity that befell them on the day of Badr do not lighten for them anything of the punishment of the Hereafter. So He said: ﴿والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾, that is: more severe. Every dāhiya (calamity) means the severe matter for which no remedy can be found. And the meaning of ﴿وَأمَرُّ﴾ is: more bitter than killing and captivity.

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُجْرِمِينَ في ضَلالٍ وسُعُرٍ﴾: it is in the exegesis that this verse was revealed concerning the Qadariyya.

zajjaj:48-48.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ في النّارِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾: the meaning is: "It will be said to them: Taste the touch of Saqar."

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿إنّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾, that is: everything We have created is decreed and written in the Preserved Tablet before it occurs. "كُلَّ شَيْءٍ" is accusative by an implied verb; the meaning is: "We have created everything; We created it by measure." This is indicated by ﴿وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ في الزُّبُرِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 52] ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وكَبِيرٍ مُسْتَطَرٌ﴾ [al-Qamar: 53]. "مُسْتَطَرٌ" is a passive participle from "اَلسَّطْرُ" (writing in lines); the meaning is: "Every sin, small and great, is recorded — written against those who do it before they do it, and written for them and against them when they do it, so that they may be recompensed for their deeds."
